questions.q: What is the Q-learning update rule?
options: Q(S_t,A_t) ← Q(S_t,A_t) + α[R_{t+1} + γ max_a Q(S_{t+1},a) − Q(S_t,A_t)]
Q(S_t,A_t) ← average of all observed returns from (S_t,A_t)
Q(S_t,A_t) ← R_{t+1} only, with no bootstrapping
questions.explain: Q-learning's update uses max_a Q(S_{t+1},a), the best possible value at the next state, as the target — not the value of the action actually taken next (that's SARSA).

options: Because it never uses exploration
Because its update target (max_a Q) estimates the value of the greedy target policy, regardless of which action the exploratory behavior policy actually took
Because it requires a known model of the environment
Because it only works on continuing tasks
questions.explain: The max_a in the update always targets the best possible action, independent of what action the agent's actual (often exploratory) behavior policy chose — this separation of behavior and target is what makes it off-policy.

questions.q: In a tabular Q-learning implementation against a Gymnasium environment, what does the epsilon-greedy branch of the code determine?
options: The TD target used in the update
The action actually taken and sent to env.step(), separate from the update's max_a target
The value of gamma used for that episode
Whether the environment is reset
questions.explain: Epsilon-greedy selects the action actually executed in the environment. The update's target, however, always uses max_a Q(next_state, a), independent of which action was actually chosen.

questions.q: What conditions are required for tabular Q-learning to provably converge to Q*?
options: The environment must be deterministic only
Every state-action pair must be visited infinitely often, and the learning rate α must be decayed appropriately over time
Epsilon must be fixed at exactly 0 for the entire training run
The reward function must always be positive
questions.explain: Under standard conditions — sufficient exploration ensuring every state-action pair is visited infinitely often, plus an appropriately decayed learning rate — Q-learning converges to the true optimal Q*.

questions.q: Once Q has converged to Q* in Q-learning, how is the optimal policy extracted?
options: π*(s) = argmax_a Q(s,a)
π*(s) is chosen uniformly at random
π*(s) = average of Q(s,a) over all actions
The optimal policy cannot be derived from Q*
questions.explain: Once Q* is known, the optimal action in any state is simply the action that maximizes Q*(s,a) — exactly the 'exploit' branch used during training.
